text: This service reads the account balance at cut-off, the COLLINS lot economics and the freshness only through the rwb-source-data contract, and keeps the FSD field names (v_ace_score.*, v_ace_account.*, v_ace_batch_status.*) as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Architecture v5, higher in source precedence, makes the 30 views readable by rwb-source-data alone; the slide 13 matrix gives S6 no cell to P1, so the path itself is open.
read: The FSD integration points and validation rules as a statement of which facts each feature needs, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 3; Section 6 FR-S6-030, FR-S6-031; Section 8.2; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S6-01
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before wave 3 system test
impact: If a view stayed readable here, the boundary test, the freshness guarantee and the masking guarantee would each need a second owner.

text: This service holds the two tables the Ownership Map names, debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account, and carries the data room state, the buyer terms, the bids, the award and the transfer as entity groups in schema rwb_debtsale until the DB story fixes their physical names.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives six things to hold; the Ownership Map and the physical schema have two tables.
read: Architecture slide 41's list as the entity set, with the physical names and field lists left to the S6 DB story.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-033; Section 8.1; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S6-02
confirm: Data architect, before the S6 DB story
impact: Five of the six records the architecture names cannot be created until the table set exists; no story is blocked from starting.

text: buyer_partner_id is a uuid business key with no foreign key, and the buyer is resolved through the S9 rwb-partner contract; the S6 migration creates no constraint that names a table outside rwb_debtsale.
why: ADR-014 and DP-01 forbid a foreign key out of the owner's schema, and the panel is S9's record.
read: The Physical Schema v6 foreign key to partner as a leftover of the single-schema monolith.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-030, FR-S6-033; Section 8.1; Section 8.4 rule 3; Section 12 OQ-S6-03
confirm: Data architect with S9, before the S6 DB story
impact: A cross-schema foreign key would couple the S6 release to the S9 schema and break the boundary test.

text: The contract is published as the API Specification v4 resources under the REST base /api/recovery/debtsale/v1, with the slide 19 /lots shorthand read as the same resource, and a staff bid read added when the contract story closes.
why: The API specification is the contract of record and the Ownership Map cites it for every S6 operation; slide 19 names the path differently.
read: Slide 19 as a shorthand design note and the API specification as the published contract.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S6-04
confirm: Solution architect, before the S6 contract story closes
impact: Two path namings would leave the gateway route and the screen client built against different contracts.

text: The buyer operations are published by this service and exposed only through the partner gateway in the DMZ, with the buyer identity and its lot scope asserted by the gateway; a buyer never reaches gateway-bff.
why: ADR-019 puts every partner user behind the partner gateway, and the buyer operations are S6's in the API specification.
read: The /partner prefix in the API specification as the partner gateway's public path, not as a second service's API.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S6-05
confirm: Solution architect with the edge owner, before wave 4 system test
impact: If S9 terminated the buyer session instead, the data room contract and the bid contract would move to S9.

text: The customer notices of a sale are sent through P6 rwb-comms from the workflow kit's Notify child, with proof of delivery recorded, and the registered-mail file goes out on P2 (INT-14); no direct WIN interface is opened here.
why: The saga and slide 26 put 'tell customers' on rwb-comms, while the FSD names WIN and the matrix gives S6 no P6 cell.
read: The FSD's 'WIN' as the physical channel behind the notice, not as a system this service calls.
applied_in: Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S6-015; Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S6-06
confirm: Solution architect with P6 and P2, before wave 4 system test
impact: A direct WIN call from this service would add an outside interface the architecture does not give it.

text: The KYC result, the licence expiry and the panel status of a buyer are held as data on the buyer record, the panel is read through the S9 contract, and the evidence the officer accepted is recorded with the admission.
why: BRD Q-011 is open and no source read names a system of record for the three facts.
read: BRD ASM-018 (the bank's existing KYC and licensing checks, held as data) as the shape of the requirement.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S6-006, CAP-S6-007; Section 6 FR-S6-009 to FR-S6-011; Section 8.2; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S6-07
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 4 release
impact: An admission decided on a fact with no owner is an admission that cannot be defended to Compliance.

text: The debt sale cap, its denominator and its period are one versioned reference-data row owned by the Head of Asset Liquidity, and the version applied is recorded at the selection, the award and the headroom report.
why: BRD Q-010 is open and the 54 percent figure alone does not define the cap.
read: BRD ASM-017 (the 54 percent applied to the eligible population of the period the policy names) as the working reading.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-002, FR-S6-029; Section 8.4 rule 1; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S6-08
confirm: Head of Asset Liquidity, before wave 4 release
impact: A cap with no denominator cannot be tested, and the headroom it reports is not a figure anyone can act on.

text: The lot approval and the award are routed through P7's approval child on the P4 delegation table, with the secured and unsecured bands of design slide 22 held as versioned reference data and the level applied and the approving role recorded on the award.
why: DL18 and BRD Q-001 leave the delegation open, and the bands exist only in a design slide.
read: Design slide 22's bands as the values in force until the delegation is signed, never as code.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-005, FR-S6-014; Section 8.4 rule 1; Section 11.3; Section 12 OQ-S6-09
confirm: Risk with the product heads, before wave 4 release
impact: An approval taken at an unversioned level cannot be reproduced, and the free-text authority column would hold a name.

text: The derecognition is this service's recorded decision and the posting and the provision input are made by P8 rwb-payment; the posted position is read back through the data path and no direct ALS or general ledger interface is opened here.
why: Architecture v5 gives S6 the activity payment.postProceeds and no cell to ALS or the general ledger.
read: R-DS-30 and R-DS-31 as decision requirements with the posting executed by the payment service.
applied_in: Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S6-020, FR-S6-021; Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S6-10
confirm: Solution architect with P8 and the ACE team, before wave 4 system test
impact: If the core bank derecognises instead, the record here becomes a confirmation rather than a decision.

text: DebtSaleWorkflow runs as the stage workflow of the case that carries the eligibility and the case-side steps and as the saga of the lot for the sale steps, with the case moved by rwb-case on LotAwarded and AccountsTransferred.
why: Slide 25 gives one child per case per stage while slide 26 and design slide 22 make the sale a saga across many cases.
read: 'One sale event closes every case in the lot' as an event requirement rather than a table write.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 7; Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S6-025 to FR-S6-027; Section 11 AC-S6-017; Section 12 OQ-S6-11
confirm: Solution architect, before the first story of the epic
impact: A per-case workflow cannot hold a lot, and a per-lot workflow cannot own a case's stage; the wrong choice is expensive to change later.

text: The sale cycle is opened by a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow on rwb-debtsale through the workflow kit, named in the job map with an owner and a run book, and the cycle date it ran for is recorded.
why: The design's monthly cycle and R-DS-01 need a trigger, and the architecture removes the shared scheduler.
read: 'Monthly cycle' as a schedule requirement, with the day of the month left as a parameter.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-028; Section 10.2; Section 11 AC-S6-001; Section 12 OQ-S6-12
confirm: Platform administrator with the solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: Without a trigger the module has no start, and a Quartz job would reintroduce the table the architecture removes.

text: LotAwarded (EV-23) and AccountsTransferred are published as CloudEvents 1.0 on rwb.debtsale.events.v1 keyed by caseId with BACKWARD-compatible schemas and no personal data, and AccountsTransferred is given its catalogue number under the same convention.
why: The event catalogue numbers LotAwarded and leaves AccountsTransferred in the unnumbered rows, and no schema exists for either.
read: The unnumbered catalogue row as an event that exists and needs a number, not as an event that may be dropped.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-026; Section 9; Section 11 AC-S6-016; Section 12 OQ-S6-13
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 4 system test
impact: Without a schema and a number the consumers cannot build, and rwb-case cannot move the case on the award.

text: The masking rules are read from P4 rwb-access as versioned policy data, the masking is applied inside this service before the tape becomes a P5 document, and the masking check is a release gate whose result is recorded on the tape record.
why: No service among the 19 performs masking, the FSD names a PII service, and NFR-041 makes the masked tape mandatory.
read: 'PII service' as the masking policy and its enforcement, not as a separate deployable.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S6-006, FR-S6-007; Section 8.4 rule 6; Section 11 AC-S6-005
confirm: Solution architect with Compliance, before wave 3 system test
impact: If masking were assumed to be someone else's service, the tape has no owner and the risk RISK-005 has no control.

text: Where the lot estimate uses an agent, it runs through the P10 rwb-agent contract with the kit's agent run, a 60 second limit and the rule result as the fallback, and the agent, model and prompt versions are recorded with the estimate; otherwise the estimate is computed from the COLLINS economics by rule.
why: R-DS-04 names a lot agent estimate and the design names a pricing agent, while no FSD feature or requirement is an agent capability.
read: The design's 'Agent run with rule fallback' as available and optional for this module, not as a required feature.
applied_in: Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S6-004; Section 9; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S6-09
confirm: Solution architect with P10, before wave 4 release
impact: If the estimate must be agent-assisted, an agent policy, a guardrail set and a measure are needed that no source currently requires.

text: The routing ladder (LOT_BUILT to LOT_CLOSED and the exception states) is the workflow state written to state, and LOV-LOT-STATUS is the business status the screen shows; both are held on the lot.
why: The routing rules and the physical schema use two vocabularies for the same lot and neither says which one the workflow writes.
read: The LOV as the screen vocabulary and the ladder as the state machine.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 8.4; Section 11 AC-S6-003
confirm: Data architect, before the S6 DB story
impact: One column written by two writers leaves the screen and the workflow disagreeing about where a lot is.

text: borrower_code and account_key are personal data in use: they are masked on every screen and on the tape and the transfer file by role, and the is_personal flag is corrected in the next version of the Logical Data Model and the physical schema.
why: Both fields identify the customer whose debt is sold, the tape leaves the bank, and the data model flags neither as personal.
read: The is_personal flag as a documentation defect rather than a decision that the field is not personal.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 8.3; Section 11 AC-S6-005; Section 11.3
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 3 system test
impact: A mask list built from the flag would leave the customer identifier in clear on an external artefact.

text: SCR-25 and SCR-26 are served by gateway-bff composite routes and PRT-05 by the partner gateway, with this service publishing only data and commands and the screen owner named in the edge story.
why: The FSD names three screens and no source read states who serves them.
read: DP-19 and the gateway notes as the routing rule for staff and partner screens.
applied_in: Section 9; Section 11.3; Section 12 OQ-S6-05
confirm: Solution architect with the edge owner, before wave 3 release
impact: An unowned screen is a screen built twice or not at all.

text: MSG-S6-001 and the four shared messages are carried in the message catalogue with a named owner and a Thai and an English version, confirmed before wave 4.
why: No source read names the owner of the wording or the approval path for a new message, and NFR-059 requires both languages.
read: FSD Appendix B as a reference to a catalogue that exists outside the sources read.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-032; Section 11 AC-S6-019; Section 12 OQ-S6-16
confirm: Business analyst, S6, before wave 4 release
impact: A message with no owner is a message that ships in one language only.

text: The four prerequisite feature codes of other modules are contract dependencies on their owning services (P7 for the rules component and the approval routing, P1 for access control per data product, P6 for the template set), and FEAT-DBS-05 and FEAT-DBS-16 are added to the dependency list when the stories are written.
why: The four are defined in other modules' FSDs, and under v5 a cross-service capability is consumed through its contract.
read: The prerequisite line as a contract dependency, never as a build dependency on another service's application story.
applied_in: Section 10.1; Section 10.3
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 release
impact: A build dependency on another service's story would hold the S6 release behind a service it does not need to wait for.

text: Every record this service holds carries a data classification and a retention class, the periods are held as reference data from DL26, and the tape and the transfer file inherit the class of the record they are derived from.
why: DL26 and BRD Q-012 are open while NFR-047 requires a classification on every record.
read: The class as the thing that must exist now, with the period as the value that arrives later.
applied_in: Section 8.1; Section 8.4 rule 7; Section 11 AC-S6-021; Section 12 OQ-S6-15
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 3 release
impact: A record with no class cannot answer a disposal or a data subject request.

text: The put-back claim window, the buyer remediation window and the settlement term are versioned reference-data values with valid-from dates, held from DL22, and the value in force at the business date of the lot is applied and recorded.
why: The rules name windows and the FSD states none of them, while DL22 makes every state service level a parameter.
read: The design's 10 working days as the value in force until the policy confirms it.
applied_in: Section 6 FR-S6-010, FR-S6-017, FR-S6-022, FR-S6-029; Section 8.4 rule 1; Section 12 OQ-S6-14
confirm: Head of Asset Liquidity, before wave 4 release
impact: A window with no value cannot be tested, and a hard-coded one cannot be changed without a release.

text: This document is version 1 of its family and stays at status Draft, with the approval table empty; the BRD approval and the Product Owner decision are treated as assumed for this run and the gate is left open for the Product Owner and the FDA.
why: No approval is recorded in the sources or in this run, and the realignment continues in Draft rather than stopping.
read: The BRD governance tables as the intended approvers rather than as completed approvals.
applied_in: Front matter (status Draft); Section 1.2; Section 13
confirm: Product Owner and FDA, at the requirements approval gate
impact: No downstream document may treat this PRD as approved until the gate is passed.

text: Every release date in this document is copied unchanged from the Program BRD release plan and marked (tentative): EP05 31 March 2027, EP06 30 April 2027, and the wave 3 releases of 28 February 2027 and 31 March 2027.
why: The realignment changes the service model, not the plan, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: The section 8 and section 10.3 dates of the Program BRD v5 as the plan of record.
applied_in: Section 10; Section 1.1
confirm: Program manager, at each release gate
impact: A reader must not treat a date here as a commitment.

text: The service is created in wave 3 and its capabilities release with EP05 in wave 3 and EP06 in wave 4; no wave conflict is raised, because the conflict rule applies only where a business epic wave is earlier than the service wave.
why: Program BRD v5 section 10.3 creates S6 in wave 3, and the E6 wave is later than it.
read: Template and Rules R5.6 as a one-directional rule.
applied_in: Section 10; Section 10.2; Section 10.3
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 release
impact: If the rule were read both ways, an unnecessary conflict row would be raised for every E6 story of this service.

text: Every CAP, FR, NFR, AC, JRN, ROL and OQ ID in this document is new to this PRD; the source IDs (REQ-S6-*, FEAT-DBS-*, R-DS-*, VR-S6-*, BR-S6-*, AC-S6-*-*, MSG-*, LOV-*, SCR-25, SCR-26, PRT-05) are preserved character for character, and BR coverage is 9 of 9 program requirements and 7 of 7 BRD requirements.
why: The module had no PRD before this run and the two requirement sets are numbered independently in their sources.
read: The Program BRD's requirement set and the E5/E6 BRD requirement set as one chain, with both IDs carried in every row.
applied_in: Section 5; Section 6; Section 11.2; Appendix A
confirm: Business analyst, S6 and the Product Owner, at the approval gate
impact: None on delivery; a reader can move from a BRD requirement to a story without a second lookup.
